doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Working for Benny Goodman
summary: Grimes found Goodman humorous and forgetful; first fully professional gig; Monk performance in the film.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: That is fantastic. And the Benny Goodman group, was that his band or was that sort of a formed band for that event.

That was his band. He had a big band for the Newport Jazz Festival, and a small group for other things we were playing. He had a quintet. Quintet maybe it was a septet. But somewhere halfway in between.
Was he interesting to work for? I’ve heard a lot of stories about him.
Oh yeah, he’s very interesting to work with. A very humorous guy.

Yeah. Certain things he’ll say, that had to make you laugh. Because I think I’m bad about remembering days, and remembering who was on them, and what was who. And he was, he’d just forget days and different occasions or knowing somebody and he’d call somebody by their name totally not who the person is. And he’d sort of go through those humorous things. But playing-wise it was very good. That was the first time I’d ever played in any completely professional — you know that was a completely professional kind of gear. So I enjoyed playing with him.
And the thing with Monk became part of the film, didn’t it?
I saw a little bit of it on a DVD.
